definition: Syndicalism means the belief that workers' unions should own and run industry.
task: Write one sentence of your own using the word syndicalism. Make the sentence show what the word means -- a reader who did not know syndicalism should be able to work it out from your sentence.

Unionism stops well short of syndicalism: the union bargains over wages and hours inside the owners' system, while syndicalism would give the union the keys to the works.

Socialism puts industry in the hands of the state or the public at large. Syndicalism agrees the private owners must go but hands the keys elsewhere: to the workers' own unions, industry by industry, with no ministry above them. The two -isms quarrel over who inherits.

In 1912, delegates from forty trades met above a printing shop to argue about who should own the future.
The older men wanted the state to buy the mills and mines; the younger ones went further in a different direction.
Their program, syndicalism, held that each industry belonged in the hands of its own workers' union -- railways to the railwaymen, mines to the miners -- with no ministry over any of them.
Skeptics in the hall asked who would settle disputes between industries if no authority stood above the unions.
The delegates never fully answered, and the movement faded, but its one big idea -- workers running their own industries -- kept resurfacing for a century.
